---
title: "How to contribute"
---

Use the [plain-language suggestion page](contributions/index.qmd). Readers submit one question, problem or proposed improvement through a structured public form. They are not expected to edit files or prepare a pull request. The [step-by-step guide](contributions/how-to-help.qmd) explains every field and shows the form after sign-in.

## What makes a useful contribution

Describe the reader’s situation, the decision or failure mode, where the change belongs, the proposed improvement and any supporting evidence. An editor will check the source, scope and implications before deciding whether work should begin.

## Privacy and licensing

Do not contribute confidential, identifiable, restricted or security-sensitive material. Prose and reusable non-code content are accepted under CC BY 4.0; code, configuration and scripts are accepted under MIT. Contributors may request named, organisational, pseudonymous or no public credit.

## Editorial outcomes

An editor may approve a suggestion, ask for evidence, defer it or decline it with a reason. Duplicate suggestions can be combined, and advice specific to one setting can be labelled as a local adaptation. Approval allows an agent to draft a change. An authorised editor then reviews that draft before it can be published.
